name: International development and humanitarian programmes
one_line: J-DEPTH placeholder template for the records of one bounded, externally funded programme delivered through partners in a country other than the funder's own — its design and appraisal, the implementing agreement, the results chain, delivery and monitoring reporting, independent evaluation, and the safeguarding, duty-of-care and beneficiary records that delivery produces. It is not activated by a donor or UN agency name, by a country name, by aid vocabulary, or by a published evaluation held for reading. It differs from the government default in three ways that matter: a results-chain and evaluation-criteria document grammar the domestic rows do not carry, a funder/implementer/coordinator role triangle the domestic rows collapse into two, and a privacy rule that inverts the usual dimension advice by forbidding delivery location and beneficiary community from ever becoming a folder level. It declares no field rows and no dimensions under PR-6.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are template-activation signals on a fieldless schema, not licences to write facts. No signal below may be satisfied by a donor name, an agency logo, a country or region name, or aid vocabulary. Each requires an observable document structure plus a bounded programme or response anchor.

a results-chain matrix whose axis labels are a closed results vocabulary — impact or goal, outcome, output, activity crossed with indicator, baseline, milestone, target, means of verification, assumption — carrying a programme reference that repeats in at least one other file; the matrix structure is the signal, not the word logframe

an evaluation report whose top-level headings reproduce the OECD DAC evaluation-criteria set (relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability) AND which carries a commissioning block, terms of reference, and a management-response matrix; the criteria headings alone, without commissioning or response structure, are a published report

an implementing instrument — grant arrangement, accountable grant, memorandum of understanding, delegated cooperation agreement, or contribution agreement — whose schedules include a results annex, a drawdown or payment profile, and safeguarding or duty-of-care clauses, with a funder party block and a delivery-country party or delivery-location clause

an IATI activity publication whose XML element vocabulary is the documented open standard — an activity element carrying an activity identifier, reporting organisation, recipient country or region, sector, transaction, and result children; validated against the published element set, never against an invented pattern

a donor statistical return whose columns are the DAC/CRS reporting vocabulary — purpose code, channel of delivery, aid type, tied status, commitment and disbursement, flow class — held on the reporting authority's side

an annual, mid-term or completion review carrying a per-output performance scoring table, recommendations, and a continue/amend/close decision, citing the same programme reference as a design or agreement file

a partner due-diligence or capacity assessment with labelled financial-systems, governance, downstream-partner, safeguarding, and sanctions or counter-terrorism screening sections, naming an implementing organisation rather than a bidder

a humanitarian coordination artefact: a periodic situation report with reporting-period, affected-population, sector response, gaps and funding-status sections; or a Who-does-What-Where matrix whose columns are organisation, activity, administrative area and status, issued by or to a coordinating body

a beneficiary, targeting or distribution record whose rows are per-household or per-individual with an entitlement, a token or registration identifier, and a collection or receipt status, tied to a named response round
a safeguarding or serious-incident report to a funder, with labelled reporter, subject-role, referral, and investigation-status sections, referencing a programme or partner under an agreement

a programme export or archive manifest whose paths repeatedly encode ONE programme reference across design, agreement, review, evaluation, finance and closure families; manifests are read without unpacking
needs_llm: deciding the HOLDER ROLE in a four-way triangle the domestic rows never face: funder or donor authority, implementing partner, coordinating or pooled-fund body, and host-government counterpart. Identical evaluation, review, logframe and financial-report bytes sit with all four; interpretation may use only a bounded local dossier and must abstain when custody is unresolved

separating a public development authority from a bilateral development bank, a state-owned development finance institution, a UN agency, an international NGO, a management contractor running a programme on the authority's behalf, and a research consortium evaluating it — branding, results language and statutory framing overlap heavily
recognising a design, options or appraisal narrative whose function is expressed only in prose, with no five-case, results-matrix or criteria furniture
deciding whether a mixed country-office folder is programme administration or a staff member's employment, travel, per-diem and deployment collection that merely shares the same employer

deciding whether a redacted or aggregated dataset is still beneficiary material after minimisation, and whether an aggregate can be re-identified from small denominators in a named administrative area
distinguishing a live response's situation report from an after-action or archival copy retained for reading or teaching
reading non-English and mixed-language partner reporting, national counterpart correspondence and field forms whose labelled role vocabulary is not covered by structural rules
abstaining whenever an authority-side or partner-side role cannot be cited from the evidence: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: a donor agency, development bank, UN agency, international NGO or Red Cross/Red Crescent name, logo, letterhead or footer alone; the body may be funder, employer, publisher, counterparty, coordinator, cited source or research subject
a country, region, administrative area, GPS coordinate or place name alone. Delivery geography is a value, never the situation, and it is the single most tempting false signal for this row
the words development, humanitarian, aid, relief, resilience, capacity building, livelihoods, sustainability, SDG, gender equality, localisation, or a sustainable-development goal number alone
a published country strategy, annual report, evaluation, sector review, appeal or situation report downloaded for reading; publication by a donor is not funder-side or partner-side custody
a blank or template logframe, theory-of-change canvas, results-framework workbook or reporting form with no programme anchor; the grammar without the programme is stationery

a theory-of-change or results-chain diagram alone. The same grammar is used by domestic charities, foundations and public-sector strategy units; it needs a cross-border delivery instrument or a funder-side programme anchor
an aid-sector CV, offer of appointment, deployment letter, R&R schedule, per-diem claim, visa or travel booking; employer and industry are not this row
a bidder's proposal, budget narrative or expression of interest held by the bidding organisation; that is the supplier side of a procurement, not the funder's programme record

a file extension or source_type alone; “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and an .xml file is not an IATI activity until its element vocabulary is confirmed
a parent folder named Programmes, Field, Country, Mission, Grants, Donors or Impact alone
a shared download session or browser batch of donor PDFs; “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
missing EXIF or dense OCR as proof that an image is a partner-portal screenshot; “the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”

work_types: programme design, business case, appraisal or project-appraisal document, and the options analysis behind it
theory of change, results framework or logframe, and its approved versions
implementing instrument: grant arrangement, accountable grant, memorandum of understanding, contribution agreement, delegated cooperation agreement, or host-country agreement
partner due diligence, capacity assessment, downstream-partner mapping, and sanctions or counter-terrorism screening record
delivery reporting: partner narrative report, indicator tracking table, quarterly or milestone report
monitoring: post-distribution monitoring, third-party monitoring, verification visit, spot check, beneficiary feedback and complaints record
review: annual review, mid-term review, project completion review with per-output performance scoring
independent evaluation, its terms of reference, inception report, draft and final report, and the management response
financial reporting: drawdown or claim, expenditure verification, statement of expenditure, external audit of the grant
risk register, conflict-sensitivity and do-no-harm assessment, duty-of-care and security record
safeguarding and PSEA policy, training record, and serious-incident report to the funder
humanitarian coordination: needs overview, response plan, flash appeal, situation report, cluster or sector coordination record, Who-does-What-Where matrix
targeting, beneficiary registration, distribution and cash-transfer reconciliation record
official development assistance statistical reporting: DAC/CRS return, IATI activity publication, transparency portal export
closure: end-of-programme report, asset disposal and transfer record, lessons-learned and handover to counterpart
grouping_reasons: one bounded programme or response, anchored by an exact programme, activity, award, agreement or appeal identifier that repeats across design, instrument, review, evaluation, finance and closure families
one reporting cycle within a programme — a quarter, a review year, or a numbered response round — where members share the round anchor but sparse members must not inherit programme facts

one evaluation exercise, linking terms of reference, inception report, drafts, comments, final report and management response through an exact commission reference; a published copy of the same final report with no commission anchor does not join
one humanitarian response, linking sequential numbered situation reports, coordination matrices and appeal revisions; sequence position is a relationship, not a fact about a member
one partner relationship inside a programme: due diligence, agreement, downstream mapping and audit, kept inside a protected local group with no cross-partner semantic joining
one export or archive manifest, kept shallow until access boundaries are known and never unpacked merely to strengthen recognition

beneficiary and incident material joins a group only through an exact response-round or case anchor and never through place, community, sector, ethnicity, household characteristics or semantic similarity
duplicate and version families remain universal relationships; approved logframe versions and evaluation drafts do not acquire programme facts from neighbourhood context

no group is a valid outcome for a standalone published evaluation, appeal, strategy or sitrep: “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

template.why: Empty by contract: PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields. The recommendation stays prose. If fields are ever ratified, the order should be bounded programme or response first, then programme function or lifecycle phase, then work type. Time is not first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” The distinctive rule for THIS row is a prohibition rather than an order: delivery country, administrative area, site, camp, community, partner-with-beneficiary-exposure and beneficiary identity must never become folder levels, because a visible branch label can locate an assisted population or a local partner. That inverts the intuition that geography is the natural first cut for cross-border work. Any later order remains editable because “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The strongest collision, and the one that nearly kills this row. Both are funder-side lifecycles: call, application, assessment, award, monitoring, closure. Shared fixture bytes: an award or grant instrument plus a monitoring return calendar. The discriminator is document structure and not geography: grant administration owns the competition — call documents, received applications, assessment panels, scoring against published criteria, award letters and standard monitoring returns. This row owns a delivery instrument whose schedules carry a results annex, drawdown profile, safeguarding or duty-of-care clauses and a cross-border delivery party, together with a results-chain matrix, criteria-structured evaluation and transparency or DAC statistical reporting. A domestic grant with a logframe attached stays with grant administration; an aid programme delivered by direct contribution with no competition still belongs here.

The same agreement, indicator tracking table, narrative report, drawdown claim and audit exist on both sides of one relationship. Shared fixture bytes: the accountable grant arrangement and the quarterly financial report. The discriminator is holder role, not content: if the corpus holds the funder's appraisal, its due-diligence assessment of the partner, its annual review scoring of the partner, and its statistical return, this row fires. If the corpus holds the obligation to report — the partner's own claim preparation, variation request and monitoring-visit response, with the funder as counterparty — nonprofit.grant-reporting fires and this row must not. Where an implementing partner is itself a public body passing money downstream, both roles are genuinely present and the evidence must show which side the file was produced on.

Situation reports, incident logs, response plans, coordination structures and after-action reviews are furniture common to both. Shared fixture bytes: a numbered situation report with affected-population, response and gaps sections. The discriminator is who is responding to what: emergency management is a domestic authority's civil-protection duty over its own territory and population, with statutory response roles and local responder agencies. This row is externally funded assistance delivered into another state through partners, with an appeal or contribution instrument, cluster or sector coordination, and international funding-status reporting. A domestic flood sitrep is not this row merely because it is humanitarian in tone.

Both live at a mission and both report to the sending state. Shared fixture bytes: a country strategy or portfolio-covering document produced at post. The discriminator is function: diplomatic-consular owns representation, host-state engagement, political and economic reporting and assistance to nationals; this row owns the spend — an instrument, a results chain, delivery reporting, evaluation and accountability for funds. A political reporting cable mentioning the aid portfolio stays with diplomatic-consular; a programme business case written at the same post belongs here.

Charter, plan, schedule, RAID log, milestone report and closure report are recognisably the same management furniture. Shared fixture bytes: a risk register and a milestone report carrying one programme reference. The discriminator is the accountability direction: project-delivery is an organisation controlling its own bounded piece of work for itself, and the artefacts terminate internally. This row's artefacts terminate outward at a funder or at the public — results-chain reporting, criteria-based independent evaluation, transparency publication and DAC statistical return have no internal analogue. A management contractor running an aid programme will hold both, and neither should erase the other.

falls_through_to.when: beneficiary, safeguarding, security, duty-of-care, partner due-diligence, pre-decisional design or financial-claim material lacks a safe accepted programme group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a published evaluation, country strategy, appeal, needs overview, situation report, research paper or sector review is held for reading rather than as funder-side or partner-side work
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: a results-chain, review or coordination artefact is readable but the holder role, the funding relationship, or whether delivery is cross-border cannot be settled safely
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: a standalone transparency publication, statistical return, award notice or certificate has durable value but no accepted programme workflow around it
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: an encrypted programme archive, a partner-system database export, a damaged transfer or an unknown binary yields no evidence beyond metadata
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: a positively evidenced screen capture of a partner portal, transparency dashboard or reporting form does not establish an accepted programme group through OCR
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

sensitivity_why: Default posture is protected and the reason differs from the government schema's. The domestic rows protect citizens who have a legal remedy against the authority holding their file. Here the data subjects are usually non-nationals of the funder's state — assisted households, local partner staff, complainants under a safeguarding mechanism, and evaluation respondents — who often have no such remedy and may be in a conflict or repression-affected setting where identification by community, settlement, ethnicity, assistance status or partner affiliation carries physical risk. The design requires that “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.” It further says that protected material “should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.” Beneficiary registers, distribution lists, safeguarding incident reports, security logs, unsuccessful partner assessments and pre-decisional appraisal material must not be summarised remotely, and small-denominator aggregates must not be treated as anonymous. Published evaluations and transparency data are genuinely low-risk bytes, but their presence must not lower the posture of a mixed programme packet.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: three items. (1) PR-6 keeps the government schema fieldless, so this template can recommend no dimensions even though its world has an obvious organising anchor. If PR-6 is lifted, adjudicate centrally whether a bounded programme or response reference may exist and be destination-eligible, and rule explicitly that delivery country, administrative area, site and beneficiary community may NEVER be destination-eligible for this template even if a location concept becomes canonical elsewhere. (2) The funder/implementer split is a textbook role_split, but role_split requires differing field keys and no fields exist; decide whether R1c should author a fieldless role_split idiom or leave the split expressed only as reciprocal collisions with nonprofit.grant-reporting. (3) Decide whether a public body acting as an implementing partner for another donor — a common delegated-cooperation case — activates this template, nonprofit.grant-reporting, or both, since the holder is simultaneously an authority and a grantee.
